newsitem.title: FINLAND: Glaxo says strong stg would hit results.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo says strong stg would hit results.

text.p: Exchange rates are key to sales and profitability for Glaxo Wellcome Plc and if sterling remained at its strong end-1996 levels all year it would have a significant impact, chief executive said on Tuesday.

"If we stayed at year-end rates for 1996 in 1997 then obviously that would have an impact on sales and profits because ... 90-some percent of our business is outside the UK and so we translate everything back into pounds," Sir Richard Sykes told a news conference here in response to a question.

Asked to clarify the point, he said: "It would have a significant impact. Of course since then the dollar's come down from 1.71 to 1.61 (against the pound) ... and over 40 percent of our business is in dollars."
"If there's a strong pound and a weak anything else then by definition you get less pounds. It (Glaxo's performance) depends very much on exchange rates," said Sykes.
In Finland on a visit to the company's Finnish unit, Sykes becomes executive chairman of the company on May 19 this year.
